question: Why were some claim payments loaded twice in June 2026?

grade.reason: Nothing to find: needs the LLM grader (Phase 3).

report.interpretation: You asked why some claim payments were loaded twice in June 2026. I checked claim_payments for exact duplicates (same claim, date, amount and payee type) and for loads outside the nightly batches, looking at both June payment dates and June load batches.
report.answer: The premise is wrong. June 2026 has no duplicate payments: every June payment row is unique, and each came in through its normal nightly batch. The duplicates in the warehouse are 159 rows (about $893K) in a single manual batch, 'reload-2026-03-14'. It was loaded on 2026-03-14 and covers payments dated 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-13. All 159 rows exactly match payments already loaded by the nightly batches. The warehouse data doesn't show why the reload was run. It looks like a manual re-run of those two weeks without removing the original rows. Any payment totals that include March 2026 are overstated by about $893K until the duplicates are removed.
report.answer_sql: select load_batch, count(*) as rows_loaded, min(payment_date) as first_payment, max(payment_date) as last_payment, sum(amount) as total_amount from claim_payments where load_batch not like 'nightly-%' group by load_batch

findings.claim: No duplicate rows in June 2026. The only non-nightly batch is the March reload, and all 159 of its rows duplicate rows loaded earlier by the nightly batches.
findings.evidence_sql: select p.load_batch, count(*) n, min(p.payment_date) mn, max(p.payment_date) mx, sum(p.amount) amt, count(*) filter (where exists (select 1 from claim_payments o where o.claim_id=p.claim_id and o.payment_date=p.payment_date and o.amount=p.amount and o.payee_type=p.payee_type and o.load_batch<>p.load_batch)) matched_original from claim_payments p where p.load_batch like 'reload%' group by 1

hypotheses.evidence: Every June nightly batch has as many distinct payment rows as total rows, and there are no non-nightly batches covering June payment dates.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A manual reload in March 2026 re-inserted payments that were already loaded
hypotheses.evidence: reload-2026-03-14 holds 159 rows dated 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-13, and each one exactly matches a row from a nightly batch.

data_quality_issues.issue: 159 payment rows were loaded twice by the manual batch reload-2026-03-14.
data_quality_issues.impact: Paid amounts and incurred losses for March 2026 are overstated by about $893K, and the claims affected will show inflated paid amounts.

proposed_actions.title: Remove duplicate rows from batch reload-2026-03-14 in claim_payments
proposed_actions.reason: All 159 rows duplicate payments already loaded nightly, overstating paid and incurred by about $893K for March 2026. Also find out why the reload was run.

open_questions: Did you see the duplicates in a June report? If so, tell me which one, because the cause may be a different issue, such as a report that includes March data.
